fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
summary: Material change since the prior snapshot is concentrated in energy supply. Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia suspended Yanbu crude loadings and cancelled some late-September European cargoes after East-West Pipeline damage, while some European physical crude cargoes rose above $130/bbl. Brent settled September 15 at $108.75 and WTI at $105.83. Libya separately halted production at Hamada, Tahara and NC5 after a pipeline-valve closure, although NOC said national output remained about 1.4 million bpd. No new official U.S., Taiwan or China macro release was incorporated in this morning snapshot. The Fed decision remains pending later September 16 and Taiwan's central-bank decision remains pending September 17.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: The dominant incremental shock is higher delivered-energy cost and physical crude scarcity. This is negative for Taiwan airlines and energy-intensive manufacturers, mixed for shipping, and adds discount-rate pressure to long-duration technology valuations. A Saudi pipeline restart within days would materially reduce this risk, but restoration timing remains uncertain.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market observations and semantic scores are research evidence only.

key_drivers.name: Saudi export disruption becomes physical cargo cancellation
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Yanbu loadings suspended and some late-September Saudi cargoes to Europe cancelled; some physical European crude cargoes exceeded $130/bbl.
key_drivers.interpretation: The disruption has moved from infrastructure risk to realized export impairment and acute physical-market scarcity.

key_drivers.name: Libya adds independent supply risk
key_drivers.observed: Libya NOC said Hamada, Tahara and NC5 were halted after the Petroleum Facilities Guard closed a pipeline valve; NOC said national production remained about 1.4 million bpd and warned force majeure was possible if disruption spread.
key_drivers.interpretation: Current aggregate loss is limited, but escalation could compound Middle East and Russian refined-product supply stress.

key_drivers.name: Fed and Taiwan central-bank event risk
key_drivers.observed: No new official decision was available in this snapshot; Fed decision is due September 16 and Taiwan central-bank decision September 17.
key_drivers.interpretation: Oil-driven inflation and bond-yield pressure keep near-term policy risk elevated.
